title: Hi, I just wanted to share my workflow with the community.
author: JedahVoulThur
selftext:
Starting with the fact that while I don't consider myself a programmer (I think the title goes to people that actually work in the field) I do have some programming knowledge and experience as a computer science professor.  

The engine I use is Godot and living in a third world country, the tools I use are completely free. Also, I released a game in 2023, mostly human made (as AI tools were very bad back then, I used ChatGPT for some design choices and online Stable Diffusion services for some art assets like UI) which gave me a lot of experience.  

  

Since then, I have been feature creeping a few projects and finishing none of them... Until the present year (2026) in which I started and finished 2 entire games, am close to finish 3 more and on early stages of 3 extra ones... I have ADHD which makes it difficult to focus on a single project and thanks to this workflow I can work, or let the AI work automatically on multiple projects, which is amazing. My GitHub profile went from a few commits per week, to around 200 per day.  

  

AI Studio

The first tool was Gemini through AI studio. I convert a GitHub repository to text using this (I am in the phone, will paste the url later) and choosing only the extensions that are important like .gd, .tres, .tscn. I avoid images but include .uid for letting the AI know that there is an image that was imported there and I untick the entire add-ons folder (In most of my projects, I use beehave, dialogue manager and GUT. More info about the last one in a moment).

My first prompt besides the text file created after the GitHub repository, is usually something like: "Analyze this Godot project and tell me what you think about it, the bugs and smells you identify".

Usually, that first response start with a very funny comment about how good the project is. I don't fall for it, that's how LLM work, but then it identifies the good and bad parts in the project. I then ask it to give me the full scripts and tscn files for solving each problem (otherwise it often just gives you a short snippet with the function to add/modify) and copy paste it into the project. I also ask it to include new or update the GUT tests, in a way that asserts every system in isolation as well as the relationships between them.

I don't talk anything about narrative, only code. I make a separate conversation without showing the code for that. 

I don't run the game or any scene before running the full GUT scripts. When the testing stops mid running, I send the error message, if it reaches 100% with red or yellow results, I ask Gemini to solve them. Only after GUT gives me a full green result, I test the scenes or entire game and take notes about the feel or small things that need fixing.

As placeholders, I use SVG art and lowpoly obj models generated by Gemini itself, I noticed it is actually pretty good at that and sometimes (like with UI, good enough to not be a placeholder but a final result).

When the conversation reaches around 800k tokens, I start the refactoring process. I send it this prompt:

(to paste later)

And it has given me amazing results. Then I repeat the process of converting the GitHub project to text, start a new conversation and continue from there.

LMArena agent mode 

  

This is what has actually multiplied my productivity.

I share my GitHub repository, tell it what my goals are and ask for a roadmap document. After revising it for a few turns, I just say "continue", "continue" multiple times. It is amazing and it's how I am able to advance with 6 parallel projects.

From time to time, I pull the GitHub repository into my computer, and run GUT. The result is often very buggy, but in no longer than 1 hour, the agent helps me reach 100% green.  

  

The first time I used this method, the agent created checks that run automatically on GitHub, but that didn't last long (remember, I am not paying a dime) so I had to tell it to instead just create GUT tests.

  

One of my projects is a strategy one, which needs heavy tunning of the factions, for balancing. Again, at first the agent run 1000 simulations itself, but after a while it could no longer do it, so I use a PowerShell command to run Godot headless the simulations and paste the results to the agent, for analyzing them and giving me ideas for how to fine-tuning (I also give my own ideas).

  

And I think that's all. As I said, I just wanted to share this workflow which is giving imho great results and making me very happy. If someone wants to share their own workflow or criticize mine, it would be great.

Thanks for reading
